Order No. 05 / Dated 14th August, 2024 Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned S.P.P. appearing on behalf of the State.

2. The petitioner is an accused in connection with Margomunda P.S. Case No.43 of 2023, registered under Sections 323, 376, 493, 506 of the Indian Penal Code and  of Dowry Prohibition Act,
pending in the Court of Learned JMFC, Madhupur.

3. It is submitted on behalf of the petitioner that the petitioner and the victim aged 18 years had been in love with each other for a period of long time and they have been living together under promise of marriage and when the petitioner deceived her to marry, the case has been instituted and therefore, there is no offence either under Section 376(2)(n) of IPC or under Section 6 of POCSO Act is made out and the petitioner is in jail since 04.04.2024 and charge-sheet has been submitted and therefore this petitioner deserves to be enlarged on bail.
4.

sentences.text: 5. Having heard the parties, perused the records of this case.
6. In the light of the allegations, it appears that this petitioner has exploited a minor tribal girl under 18 years of age for a long period of time.
The petitioner used to tease and outrage her modesty when the victim being minor tribal girl used to go to her school.

Further it has been alleged that the petitioner took the victim girl forcibly to his house under the pretext of marriage but later on he refused to marry with her when the petitioner and his family members started demanding dowry while it has come into evidence that the father of the victim girl had died long back and she was mentally and physically exploited by this petitioner due to her poverty and helplessness.
Paragraphs 3, 4, 5, 6, 10 and 33 of case diary has fully supported the case of prosecution.

In this case,
charge-sheet has been submitted for the offence punishable under Sections 323, 376(2)(n) & 506 of the Indian Penal Code and Section 6 of the POCSO Act and charge is yet to be framed and therefore under the circumstances of the case it is not found just and fair to enlarge the petitioner on bail at this stage of the case inasmuch as the possibility of threatening or winning over the witnesses cannot be ruled out.
7. In view of this matter, this Court does not find fit to enlarge the petitioner on bail.

Accordingly,
the prayer of the petitioner for the grant of bail is hereby rejected.

(Navneet Kumar, J.) Basant/S. Das Bablu Hembrom @ Bablu Hembram vs The State Of Jharkhand on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143136104/
